Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested eight members of a transnational drug trafficking cartel accused of moving cocaine from Lagos through Kano, Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. The suspects, who allegedly swallowed cocaine pellets to evade security checks, excreted a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilogrammes while in NDLEA custody. The agency said the suspects were arrested during intelligence-led operations in Lagos and Kano between October 30 and 31, 2026. In a statement on Tuesday, the NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, said the operation began with the arrest of a 57-year-old suspect, Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos, on October 30. The statement partly read, “Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have dismantled a transnational drug trafficking cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the desert via Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. As a result, eight members of the syndicate were arrested in well-coordinated intelligence-guided operations in Lagos and Kano. “All eight suspects who were nabbed between Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October 2026 were drug mules who had swallowed cocaine pellets, excreting a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilograms over several days in custody. Add us to your Preferred Sources “The operation began on Friday 30th October when operatives of a Special Operations Unit of the Agency arrested the first suspect, 57-year-old Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos. He later excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650kg. “The next day, Saturday October 31, four more members of the cartel were stopped at the MM2 Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano. They are: Jackson Ahamefule, 43, who excreted 90 wraps weighing 1.950kg; Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47, who excreted 85 wraps weighing 1.750kg; Marcel Nnabuike, 38, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.655kg; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.650kg.” Babafemi said the five suspects arrested in Lagos excreted a combined 399 wraps of cocaine weighing 8.655kg. He said intelligence gathered during the Lagos operation indicated that other members of the cartel had travelled to Kano, prompting NDLEA operatives at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport to intercept them at the domestic terminal. The three suspects arrested in Kano were identified as Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31. He said body scans confirmed that the suspects had swallowed drugs, adding that they were placed under observation until they excreted the cocaine pellets. The statement said Ifechukwu excreted 85 pellets weighing 1.853kg, Nwaorji expelled 80 pellets weighing 1.752kg, while Chinaka excreted 70 pellets weighing 1.535kg. It added that the suspects disclosed that they planned to travel by road from Kano through Niger Republic and Libya, with Europe as their final destination. Reacting to the arrests, the NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), commended operatives of the agency’s Special Operations Unit and Kano command for the operation. Marwa said, “Their intelligence-driven synergy, speed and professionalism ensured that not one of the eight mules slipped through our net between Lagos and Kano.” He added, “This cartel thought it had found a back door to Europe through our northern borders and the Sahara. Their arrests are a message to drug barons and their couriers that there is no safe route out of Nigeria. “Whether they go by air, by road or through the desert, we will trace them, find them and bring them to justice.” The NDLEA boss also warned young people against allowing drug traffickers to use them as couriers. “Swallowing wraps of cocaine is a death wish. One burst pellet can kill a mule before the journey ends. No amount of money is worth that risk,” he warned.
